ut_ewe_for_real_wall.blurb: A compact desert wall at the southern end of the Ibex area in Utah's West Desert, part of the Corral Crags group. It holds a dozen routes, mostly bolted with a few trad lines, running from easy climbing up to low 5.12, with the bulk in the middle grades. The routes are short, so it suits a quick session of single-pitch leading rather than a long day. Some lines have a mixed character, and anchors are in place on nearly all of them, which makes lowering off simple.

ut_temple_quarry.blurb: A small cluster of boulders at the mouth of Little Cottonwood Canyon in the Wasatch, on the south side of the road near the old quarry trail. Twelve problems are known, running from an easy V0 up to about V5, with most in the V3 to V4 band, so it favours climbers who already move well on moderate boulders. Some of the best problems are chunky blocks with arêtes, seams and traverses. The boulders sit close to the parking area, so it works for a short session or a warm-up before heading deeper into the canyon.

ut_ice_wall_the.blurb: A sport wall in Ogden Canyon, in the northern Wasatch, with twelve routes. Eleven are bolted lines graded from 5.10 to 5.12, with the largest group at 5.11, and there is a single aid line. It is a place for climbers who are already comfortable leading in the 5.10s and up rather than a beginner crag. The routes are clustered together on one wall, so a day here is easy to organise around a short list of lines.

ut_road_boulder.blurb: A single sandstone boulder in the New Joe's section of Joe's Valley in central Utah, holding twelve problems from V0 to V4. Most are on the easy side, with five at V1, a few V3s and a pair of V4s, so it works well as a warm-up stop or a place for newer boulderers. The rock is fairly clean with interesting features, the landings are flat, and the faces are only mildly steep. A vertical splitter crack divides the boulder, and some problems finish on top with an easy way back down.

ut_river_road_dihedrals.blurb: A small wall on the River Road north of Moab, on the sandstone of southeast Utah. It offers twelve routes that mix cracks with face climbing, split between trad and sport. Most of them sit around 5.9, with just a few harder lines reaching into the 5.11s and one at 5.12, so it suits climbers looking for moderate crack and face practice close to the road. Because it is small, it makes a handy short stop rather than a full-day destination.

ut_ammo_dump_wall.blurb: A steep sport wall in Box Canyon, a side of Maple Canyon in central Utah. All twelve routes are bolted, and the wall leans out at roughly 30 degrees, so the climbing is sustained and physical. Grades are weighted toward the upper end: one easy line near 5.8, a few at 5.11, about half at 5.12, and a couple of 5.13s. That makes it a good fit for strong sport climbers wanting to push on overhanging terrain, though there is little here for beginners.

ut_bat_cave_throne_grease_boulders.blurb: A group of boulders beneath a small cliff band near the Cart Bridge boulders at Flaming Gorge in northeast Utah. The rock is quartzitic sandstone. Twelve problems are known and the spread is wide, from V0 up to V10, though most of them are V5 and harder, so it leans toward strong boulderers. The Bat Cave has an overhanging roof, and the Grease boulder carries one of the hardest lines. The boulders sit close together, which keeps the circuit compact.

ut_blank_cave_the.blurb: Sunset Alley, near St. George in southwest Utah, holds this cave on the canyon's left. All twelve climbs are sport routes with a very steep, powerful feel and a wide grade range: from about 5.9 up to 5.14, with the heaviest concentration at 5.13. The left end offers a few easier routes that work as a warm-up before moving to the harder lines. A fair number of the cave's lines are still unfinished projects, so this is mostly a place for experienced sport climbers.
